question: Is column permutation uniform, and does uniqueness rejection preserve its conditional law?
outcome: Enumerated 8,000 balanced binary tables and 2,880 unique tables; exact acceptance .36 and equal generating multiplicities. All 2,880 unique tables have full nested fits; exact 5% nested rejection is 5%.
challenge: Tiny ordinary tables can have too few components for the preserved five-fold procedure.
remedy: Count the full ordinary space without inventing nested scores; fit the unique subset and retain the domain issue for a separate declared experiment.
retry_when: A changed observation law, statistic or conditional constraint supplies a new finite space.

question: How does record-wise shuffling behave under a known literal-copy process?
outcome: Four latent binary objects give 216 tables. With three copies each, an integer adjacency test rejects 25% at nominal 5% under record-column tails; matched object tails reject 2.78%. Exact distributions retained for one through five copies.
challenge: Ordinary record references mostly leave the copy-supported table space.
remedy: Enumerate latent tables and count expanded reference scores with integer convolution; an independent row-state dynamic program checks every distribution and tail.
retry_when: Known unequal-copy or nonidentical-face mechanisms change the supported observation space.

question: Can a reference preserve both latent and expanded margins with unequal copy counts?
outcome: For multiplicities 1,1,1,2,2,3, fixing three latent and five expanded ones leaves six columns. Integer continuation sampling gives exact uniform 1/6 column probabilities. Direct and rejection streams each preserve 100,000 sampled tables.
challenge: Unrestricted object shuffles change expanded margins in fourteen of twenty columns. The direct stream has a retained .01336 chi-square diagnostic.
remedy: Count legal completions exactly, verify every branch probability and independently replay streams. Preserve the uneven sample diagnostic beside the exact law.
retry_when: An established copy process has additional count/stratum constraints requiring a new conditional sampler.

question: Does deduplicating raw draws give the same law as drawing a population conditional on uniqueness?
outcome: Seven binary draws retained as six unique balanced strings have four unequal support masses. Uniform-reference nested rejection becomes 5.1537% at nominal 5%; matched selected-law tails give 4.9407%. No model refits were needed.
challenge: Whole-string uniqueness alone does not specify the raw selection history.
remedy: Specify the raw process, sum exact occupancy probabilities, reuse frozen scores and check support weights by an independent seen-set recurrence and every weighted tail.
retry_when: A proposed catalogue selection history supplies a different explicit inclusion law.

question: Can whole ordered face vectors preserve a known paired-error law in the nested reference?
outcome: Across 1,000 twenty-object populations, matched vector references reject 5% at nominal 5%, versus 11% for record-wise references; paired excess 6 points, interval 4.3–7.7. All 198,000 reference corpora and fifteen full fit replays audited. Two finite spaces and 200,000 sampler draws independently checked.
challenge: Scalar record shuffling preserves marginals while changing every tested joint vector margin. Physical/text aliases can also create fitting-domain failures outside sampled main trials.
remedy: Condition on ordered-vector counts, preserve physical aliases, rebuild fit components on every proposal, use disjoint seed namespaces and preserve a separate support-domain witness.
retry_when: An independently justified observer-error kernel, vector structure or archaeological relation changes the stated sampling model.

question: How do undefined fits, score extension and feasibility conditioning change reference rejection fractions?
outcome: Same vector margins permit one or twenty components; one-component nested fit raises ZeroDivisionError. Across all 8,000 binary tables, a zero-gain extension with observed abstention rejects 400 at nominal 5%, or 6.9444% among 5,760 usable observations. Conditioning the reference on usability rejects 276/5,760, or 4.7917%.
challenge: A uniform table sampler does not by itself define a statistic on every supported table. Reporting only feasible observations changes the measured population.
remedy: Preserve the failed fit and declare extension/selection alternatives before their exact evaluation. Independently check every graph, full tail, conditional tail and selected fit replay.
retry_when: A prospective corpus needs a declared total statistic or an explicit feasible-observation selection law.

question: Can paired faces estimate a known symmetric error rate and correct latent frequencies?
outcome: On 1,000 frozen populations with true rate .1, agreement and joint mean estimates are .099261 and .101605. Known-rate inversion gives 10,335 negative components, matching exact expectation 10,331.87. Small-cell total variation is .245280 for joint correction and .227690 for matched shrinkage; pooled correction improves .020967 to .012236. Exact identification limits retained.
challenge: Finite inversion can leave the simplex; a flexible corrected estimator can still lose to a prior-matched simple baseline. An unspecified boundary fallback was found, with no main case using it.
remedy: Constrain the fit, retain matched shrinkage, compute exact absence/agreement distributions, audit all objectives/projections and preserve the boundary note without changing endpoints.
retry_when: A new kernel, correlated observers or near-uniform latent frequencies provide an explicit misspecification or identification test.
